items.followUp: Name two hormones produced by the pancreas and state their effect on blood glucose.

rubric.why: Identifies the liver’s role in storing glucose as glycogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver stores glycogen.

rubric.why: Identifies the liver’s role in maintaining blood glucose levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver regulates blood glucose or blood sugar.

rubric.why: Identifies the liver’s role in breaking down harmful substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver detoxifies harmful substances.

rubric.why: Identifies the liver’s role in converting excess amino-acid nitrogen into urea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning urea production or formation by the liver.

rubric.why: Rewards a correct explanation of how the liver helps regulate blood glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that excess glucose is stored as glycogen and glycogen can be converted back to glucose.

modelAnswer: The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen.
When blood glucose falls, the liver converts stored glycogen back into glucose, helping regulate blood glucose.
It converts excess amino-acid nitrogen into urea.
Any four functions may be given; the glucose-storage and glucose-regulation statements describe one function in detail.

items.followUp: Name two steps of the biological method used to investigate a biological problem.

rubric.why: Describes the biological method as an organised approach.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a systematic method, approach or way.

rubric.why: States what the biological method is used for.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it is used to investigate or solve biological problems.

modelAnswer: The biological method is a systematic approach to investigating and solving biological problems.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of drawing a conclusion at the end of an investigation?

rubric.why: Identifies reporting results as the final stage of the biological method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that reporting results is the final or last step.

rubric.why: Explains that investigation findings are communicated to others.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that results are communicated, for example through a report or publication.

modelAnswer: Reporting the results is the final step of the biological method.
The scientist communicates the findings and conclusion, usually in a scientific report or publication, so others can learn about the investigation.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example of it in a living organism.

rubric.why: Identifies filtration as a process used to separate components of a mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that filtration separates particles from a fluid.

rubric.why: Describes how a filter separates particles from a fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the fluid passes through a filter while particles are retained.

modelAnswer: Filtration is the process of separating suspended or insoluble particles from a fluid by passing the mixture through a porous filter.
The fluid passes through the filter while particles too large to pass through are retained.
